slides.title: Introduction Dianalyzer
slides.body:
DIAnalyzer is the diagnostic
tool that use FCA.
At the moment the actual
version is 4.x.
This version is quite similar
to CDA that is the
diagnostic tool of Chrysler.
It’s necessary the login to
use it (it’s necessary the
authorization).
It’s possible to use it in
Offline mode («Offline
Authentication») but it’s
necessary a specific
authorization.
IntroductionDianalyzer -

slides.title: Selection Hardware
slides.body:
Options sheet🡪 Hardware: it’s
possible explore the hardware
setting windows for each CAN
bus.
The selection of hardware
and channel of the hardware
is the first step to configure
the correct communication
between ECUs and
DIAnalyzer.
Note: the setting about the
communication are depending
from the hardware and from
the used CAN bus 🡪 for
example, in this case, the
ECM communicates with the
Vector CancaseXL on channel
2 Highspeed.
SelectionHardware

slides.title: Selection Car
slides.body:
DIAnalyzer 4.x.x has a
database with the .car file;
these are the configuration
file for a specific
vehicle/project of FCA.
The user has to select the
.car of the project that is
going to check:
File 🡪 Open 🡪 (select .car
in the folder Config of
DIAnalyzer)
SelectionCar

slides.title: Screen Main
slides.body:
After the selection of the
.car, DIAnalyzer fill the
three sheets signed in red
for the specific project:
Car 🡪 in this section is
shown all ECU of the
vehicle in reference to the
selected CAN bus.
ECUs 🡪 in this section it’s
possible view all the
vehicle’s ECU (like as CDA)
Bus 🡪 DIAnalyzer shows all
the accessible bus of the
vehicle.
ScreenMain

slides.title: Main Screen ECU
slides.body:
If all hardware connection are
correct, the communication
starts. In the figure it’s possible
to check the Dianalyzer request
(Tx messages) and the ECU
response (messages Rx). In this
case the response is positive.
On the left side of each framte
it’s possible to check:
- Communication timing for
each frame
- ECU that are communicationg
(who is the sending? Who is
the receiver)
Main ScreenECU
It’s possible to start the diagnostic communication between DIAnalyzer and a specific ECU clicking on
the ECU for the selected bus 🡪 the image below shows the connection with the TCM (Transmission
Control Module, this is the ECU that it’s necessary for each vehicle equipped with a non manual
transmission).

slides.title: Generic Command ECU
slides.body:
Generic CommandECU -
When the user selects the
.car file, it’s start the
diagnostic communication
with the ECU. DIAnalyzer
upload in automatic way
the .PAR file that it’s
necessary to decode the
raw value exchanged
between ECU and
DIAnalyzer.
«Load PAR File» button
needs to change the
decryption file (it’s
necessary to decode the
diagnostic information for
each ECU).
«Stop» button needs to stop the communication between
DIAnalyzer and the selected ECU. If the user presses the
button, this button change the name in «Start»; in that case,
the selection of this button needs to restart the communication
with the ECU.
«Extended» button needs to switch between the many
diagnostic sessions that are necessary to interact with
the ECU: Default / Extended.

slides.title: Screen Overview of all
slides.body:
ScreenOverview of all
Screen 1 – Generic Command
Generic screen, it’s possible
read the communication
«trace» and it’s possible to
send any kind of request to
the ECU in raw format (in this
screen it’s possible read the
raw response of the ECU).
Screen 2 – ECU
Identifications
In this screen DIAnalyzer
shows the ECU
identification parameters,
like SW number, HW
number, ISO code, etc...
Screen 3 – Diagnostic
Trouble Codes
Here, DIAnalyzer shows all the stored
DTC (Diganostic trouble code); there
are all the stored DTC in the
diagnostic memory of the ECU; there
are also the state and details of each
error like snapshot and extended data
record.
Screen 4 – Parameter
Reading
DIAnalyzer shows all the RDBI
(Read data by Identifier)
necessary for diagnostic
analysis. The RDBI are called
also engineering paramenters
Screend 5 – Active
Diagnosis
DIAnalyzer can command many
actuators to perform an active diagnosis
with IOCBI function (Input Output Control
by identifier).
Screen 6 – EOL
Programming (PROXI)
In this panel it’s possible to
perform the ECU personalization
procedure (PROXI).
Screen 7 – Cyber
Security
Screen 9 –
Download
In this panel
it’s possible
to perform a
software
download on
the ECU.

slides.title: ECU Software Download Screen 9 –
slides.body:
To update an ECU with DIAnalyzer it’s
necessary the presence of three different
file: .idx, .prm e .bin.
The user has to put these three file (with the
same name but with different extension) in
the same folder.
The procedure for the software download is:
o Press «File IDX»: select the file located
on the PC;
o DIAnalyzer select in an automatic way
the other two files.
o If DIAnalyzer can’t select the .bin and the
.prm, the user can perform this operation
in manual mode;
o The user has to press the Download
button;
o DIAnalyzer shows the progress of the
download procedure and it shows a
popup message when the procedure has
terminated.
Note: it’s possible to open the .idx file with a
text editor to check the content.
ECU Software DownloadScreen 9 –

slides.title: PROXI procedure 1\3 Screen 6 –
slides.body:
PROXI procedure.
FCA requires the development of a software
general purpose to his software supplier. FCA
requires to develop a software that can be
customizable (for different engine,
transmission and optional). FCA requires a
software that can manage or not any kind of
functionality; in that way, the supplier can
develop only one software and FCA can
personalize this software in the production site
(PROXI procedure).
The PROXI procedure is a configuration
process: with the PROXI the use can
activate/deactivate many functionalities during
the EOL (End Of Line) process; for example
the use can personalize the vehicle
with/without Stop&Start, with
manual/automatic climate control, gear ratio
and other functionalities.
Screen PROXI – it’s reccomand to access
using the icon PROXI in the CAR screen.
The use can perform the PROXI procedure in
KeyOn (it’s not possible perform the
procedure in Engine Running).
Only the qualified users can perform the
PROXI procedure.
Each vehicle has his configuration file: in the
configuration file there are all the features of
the vehicle.
The configuration file is stored in the BCM
and a backup copy is located in the IPC
PROXI procedure 1\3Screen 6 –

slides.title: PROXI procedure 2\3 Screen 6 –
slides.body:
PROXI procedure 2\3Screen 6 –
Car Alignment:
The user can command
the BCM to force the
PROXI on all vehicle
ECU: in the specific, the
BCM provides the
personalization
command (they are
present in the
configuration file) to all
ECU of the vehicle.
Read Proxi BCM:
With this command the user can read
the configuration file of the vehicle and
he can save this file with the extension
.byt.
This functionality is possible only in the
vehicle because it’s necessary tre
presence of a real BCM. In any case it’s
possible also read the configuration file
from the IPC
Open EOL File:
This functionality is useful to work in a
simulated environment (e.g. HiL simulator
or stati bench). It an user saved a
configuration file from a real BCM, it’s
possible to save it with extension .byt and
it’s possible open and modify.

slides.title: PROXI procedure – Example Screen 6 –
slides.body:
It’s necessary the next step:
o Upload of a .PAR file for the
specific project 🡪
o Upload of a .byt file with the
button «Open EOL File».
In the example there’s the results of
the operation described above:
o In the lower section of the screen
there’re the decoding of the .byt
file content; here there are all the
activable features of the ECU
o It’s possible to modify the
activable features of the ECU
using the button «Change Proxi»
o It’s useful save each time the .byt
file with a different name; you
can distinguish between the
original configuration and the
new ones.
